rules.rationale: Rigid polycyclic solutes form poor aqueous cavities, so hydration is disfavored relative to flexible polar chains.
Acyclic solutes reorient freely to expose hydrogen-bonding groups to water, lowering hydration free energy.
Extended aromatic surfaces are hydrophobic and solvophobically penalized, weakening net aqueous affinity.
Branching buries polar functionality, reducing solvent-accessible heteroatom area available for hydration.

skills.hypothesis: Structure-shape rules transfer: ring-free, unbranched solutes hydrate better because polar groups stay solvent-exposed. It may fail for polar heterocycles where ring nitrogens or oxygens hydrogen-bond strongly.

rules.rationale: Many heteroatoms give strong H-bond and dipole interactions that stabilize the aqueous phase.
Pure hydrocarbon character lacks polar contacts, so hydration is entropically and enthalpically disfavored.
Short SMILES track small polar solutes with favorable exposure of hydrogen-bonding groups to water.
Longer scaffolds add hydrophobic surface and conformational cost that weaken net hydration.

skills.hypothesis: Heteroatom density drives hydration free energy through hydrogen bonding and polarity; it may fail when intramolecular hydrogen bonds shield polar groups or when aromatic rings dominate.

state.lesson: The ring/structure counter-hypothesis reached higher mean development AUC (82.3 vs 69.7) across eight seeds with comparable final best, so shape-based hydrophobicity rules transfer better than the heteroatom-only prior on this target; the spread across seeds is wide, so confidence stays moderate rather than high.
state.revision_summary: Promoted the counter-hypothesis structure skill to deployment on the strength of its development AUC, dropped the near-duplicate aromatic_none rule, added an aromatic_high face penalty, and retained the heteroatom polarity prior as the alternative.
